description:
The surah that opens with admonishing the Prophet and refers to him as **He [who] Frowned** and turned away. While the Prophet was speaking to some unbelieving nobles of Quraysh, hoping to convert them, a blind Muslim man came up to learn from him, but in his eagerness to attract the disbelievers to Islam, the Prophet frowned at him. The Prophet is then reproached and told not to concern himself with the disbelievers. It takes its name from the word "he frowned" ('abasa) in verse 1. The surah also deals with the condemnation of man's ingratitude: man becomes self-satisfied and forgets his origin and his final return to God.
The surah is also known as He Made a Wry Face, He Who Frowned

or take admonition,

translations.5: But as for someone who is self-complacent,
translations.7:

translations.8: But he who comes hurrying to you,
translations.11: No indeed! These [verses of the Qur'ān] are a reminder
translations.12: —so let anyone who wishes remember it—
translations.17: Perish man! How ungrateful is he!
translations.18: From what has He created him?
translations.19:
He has created him from a drop of [seminal] fluid,
  and then proportioned him.
translations.20: Then He made the way easy for him;
translations.21: then He made him die and buried him;
translations.22: and then, when He wished, resurrected him.
translations.23:
No indeed! He has not yet carried out
  what He had commanded him.
translations.24: So let man observe<{["F", 1]}> his food:
translations.26: then We split the earth into fissures
translations.27: and made the grain grow in it,
translations.32: as a sustenance for you and your livestock.
translations.33: So when the deafening Cry comes
translations.34: —the day when a man will evade his brother,
translations.37:
that day each of them will have
  a task to keep him preoccupied.
translations.38: That day some faces will be bright,
translations.40:
And some faces on that day
 will be covered with dust,
translations.42: It is they who are the faithless, the vicious.<{["F", 1]}>
